# The Shadow That Proves the Light

## Scripture

"Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows." — James 1:17

## Reflection

In September, as Earth drifts through the debris trail of an ancient comet, the Orionids begin their quiet streaking across the pre-dawn sky. But there's something else happening these nights—Earth passes through the edge of our planet's shadow more noticeably, and the stars seem to sharpen, as if polished by the cooling air.

Here's what astronomers remind us: we only see shadows because light exists. A shadow isn't the absence of light's source—it's evidence that something stands between us and the brightness. James uses this imagery deliberately. He calls God the "Father of the heavenly lights," then contrasts Him with "shifting shadows." Everything in creation casts shadows, changes, fades. The moon waxes and wanes. Constellations drift. Even starlight, traveling for millennia, eventually dims.

But God doesn't shift. His character casts no varying shadow because there is no turning in Him. When autumn's shortening days feel like encroaching darkness, remember—shadows prove the sun still shines. Your seasons of waiting, of grief, of uncertainty are not evidence that God has withdrawn. They are shadows cast by His constant light, reminding you that something bright stands just beyond your view.

The One who set every star in motion holds you with the same steady hand.

## Prayer

Father of heavenly lights, when life feels shadowed and uncertain, remind me that shadows only exist because Your light remains. You do not shift or change. Anchor my heart in Your constancy, and let every dark season draw me closer to the brightness of Your presence. Amen.
